facts.statement: The genus Fluvioviridavis was first described by Mayr in 2005.
The genus Fluvioviridavis was originally named by Mayr and Daniels in 2001.
The type species of the genus Fluvioviridavis is Fluvioviridavis platyrhamphus.
Two other species, F. michaeldanielsi and F. nazensis, were described by Mayr and Kitchener in 2024.
facts.quote: subdivision: F. michaeldanielsi Mayr & Kitchener, 2024 F. nazensis Mayr & Kitchener, 2024

facts.statement: Fluvioviridavis is the sole genus in the monotypic family Fluvioviridavidae.
facts.quote: Fluvioviridavis is the only genus currently named in the monotypic family Fluvioviridavidae.

facts.statement: Fossils of Fluvioviridavis have been found in the Early Eocene Green River Formation in Wyoming and the London Clay Formation in the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Fluvioviridavis is an extinct genus of bird from the Early Eocene Green River Formation of Wyoming (United States) and London Clay Formation of the United Kingdom.

facts.statement: Fluvioviridavis lived during the Ypresian stage, between 56 and 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are five recorded fossil occurrences of Fluvioviridavis in the Paleobiology Database.

rejected.statement: Fluvioviridavis is classified within the class Aves.
